title: Chatflow concurrency & surge-fuzz emulator for streaming completions (SSE/WebSocket)
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Create a deterministic, configurable emulator that reproduces long-tail and bursty streaming chat workloads across SSE and WebSocket transports. The goal is to detect p95 regressions and functional regressions in streaming behavior (connection drops, backpressure, partial payloads) when we change kernel scheduling, batching heuristics, or KV cache behaviors. This emulator must support: configurable client mixes (idle/bursting/long-poll), realistic token emission rates per-session, CV/seeded randomness for reproducible runs, and an option to replay recorded production traces with injected network jitter and connection churn.
acceptance_criteria:
- Emulator can synthesize 100k concurrent virtual sessions across both SSE and WS protocols with controllable latency and token-rate distributions.
- Emit metrics for tokens/sec (global and per-tenant), active_connections, p95/p99 stream-completion latency, connection_failure_rate, partial_response_rate, and kv_cache_warm_ratio.
- CI gate that fails if p95 increases by >10% versus baseline or if connection_failure_rate > 0.5% for a sustained 5m window.
- Reproducible run: seed + manifest -> identical token/time traces across runs.
- Integrations: dashboard panels (perf + error), a GitHub action that runs a gated smoke run, and a canary pipeline for Dedicated clusters.
implementation_notes:
- Core emulator written in Go for low GC overhead; worker model spawns lightweight goroutines to emulate clients and uses HTTP/2 multiplexing for efficient connections where appropriate.
- Streaming transports: use the same production client libs to exercise identical code paths (SSE client, native WS client).
- Token emission modeled as a hierarchical generator: session-level profile (mean tokens/sec, burst probability, sequence length distribution) and message-level template (golden prompts for warm-start tokens and real recorded prefixes).
- KV-cache awareness: sessions can be flagged as warm (replay of prior prefixes) or cold to measure benefit variance. Add headers to requests to ensure runtime picks the same execution kernels.
- Provide a "surge-fuzz" mode that randomly spikes a subset of clients to very high token rates to exercise scheduler preemption and backpressure.
- Metrics export via Prometheus; attach labels for model, runtime-variant, and test-seed.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for generator determinism and token schedule correctness.
- Small local end-to-end with 1k concurrent sessions to validate p95/kpi wiring and log formats.
- Staging runs: 10k, 50k, 100k virtual sessions across two transport mixes (50/50 and 90/10 SSE/WS) to capture scaling curves.
- Regression detection: baseline snapshot collected from last green run stored in S3. New runs compare p95 and tokens/sec curves; build a time-series delta report and raise PR comment with trend chart.
- Chaos knobs: simulate network latency gradients (0-250ms), TCP resets, and client reconnect storms. Ensure emulator can replay recorded production trace files with optional jitter injection.
